newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Dragonair cancels seven flights.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Dragonair cancels seven flights.

text.p: Hong Kong Dragon Airlines Ltd (Dragonair) said it had cancelled seven flights and rescheduled eight on Saturday due to the suspension of its four Airbus Industrie A330-300 aircraft.
"A total of 15 flights are being affected today. Of them, seven have been cancelled and passengers are being arranged to take flights of other airlines," a spokeswoman for the airline told Reuters.
"The eight others have been rescheduled," she said.
She gave no information on the affected flights.
Anthony Philips, another spokesman for Dragonair, told Reuters the suspended aircraft mainly served routes to Beijing, Shanghai, Kaohsiung and Xiamen.
Earlier on Saturday, Dragonair said it has suspended operations of its four A330-300 aircraft due to concerns about the reliability of their Rolls-Royce Trent 700 engines.
The spokeswoman said the suspension also led to the downgrading of seats for some passengers as some routes of the A330-300 aircraft was served by A-320 aircraft.
A330-300 aircraft had first-class and economy-class seats, while A-320 aircraft had a configuration of either a combination of business and economy seats, or only economy seats, she said.
Swire Pacific Ltd and Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd together hold about 26 percent of Dragonair, whose major shareholder is China National Aviation Corp.
